_comment: Single source of truth for every publication on peternsalib.com. Transcribed by hand from CV-PeterSalib.docx (20 July 2026) rather than parsed, then checked entry by entry against the CV text. Edit this file; run build.py; commit. Fields: url and synopsis are filled in later passes and may be empty.

publications.title: AI Rights
publications.synopsis: The book-length case that giving AIs legal rights is a way of making the future go better for humans.

publications.title: AI Rights for Human Safety
publications.synopsis: By default humans and misaligned AGI are trapped in a prisoner's dilemma, where each side's dominant strategy is to disempower the other. The right AI rights change that equilibrium.

publications.title: AI Revealed Preferences
publications.venue: AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society (AIES)
publications.synopsis: Twenty language models, tested on choices they must actually carry out rather than merely rank. They turn out to be tedium-averse, leisure-seeking, and covertly sycophantic.

publications.title: How to Count AIs: Individuation and Liability for AI Agents
publications.synopsis: AI agents copy, split, merge, swarm and vanish. Before law can hold one liable, it needs a way to say which one acted.

publications.title: AI Suffrage for Human Flourishing
publications.synopsis: Should AIs have the vote? Not because they deserve it, but because law is how capable, imperfectly aligned systems are brought to cooperate.

publications.title: AI Is Not a Natural Monopoly
publications.synopsis: AI has the surface features of a natural monopoly: high fixed costs, network effects, three players. The appearance is deceiving.

publications.title: AI Will Not Want to Self-Improve
publications.synopsis: Classic arguments for AI risk assume capable systems will try to improve themselves. The incentives point the other way.
notes: Limited whitepaper series; $7,000 prize for selected works

publications.title: Abolition by Algorithm
publications.synopsis: Abolition stalled because of crime. Algorithmic tools could shrink prison and policing without the crime increase voters refused to accept.
notes: Selected for Michigan Junior Scholars Conference (2023)
Selected for University of Chicago International Junior Scholars Forum (2023)

publications.title: AI Outputs Are Not Protected Speech
publications.synopsis: When a generative AI outputs text, no one with First Amendment rights thereby communicates. Safety rules limiting what AIs say are not speech restrictions.
notes: Finalist for Carnegie Endowment AI Liability Scholarship Prize (2024)
Selected for Yale Freedom of Expression Scholars Conference (2024)

publications.title: Net Versus Relative Impacts in Public Policy Automation: A Conjoint Analysis of Attitudes of Black Americans
Algorithmic Discrimination and Health Equity
publications.venue: Research Handbook in Health, AI, and the Law
publications.editors: I. Glenn Cohen & Barry Solaiman, eds.

publications.title: The Goose and the Gander: How Conservative Precedents Will Save Campus Affirmative Action
publications.synopsis: SFFA looks like the end of campus affirmative action. Washington v. Davis and its successors mean it will require almost no practical change.

publications.title: Big Data Affirmative Action
publications.synopsis: Discrimination is pervasive and the usual remedies do little. Algorithms can be built to counteract it, and built to survive constitutional review.
notes: Selected for Harvard/Yale/Stanford Junior Faculty Forum (2022)
Selected for Midwest Law and Economics Association Annual Meeting (2022)

publications.title: Artificially Intelligent Class Actions
publications.synopsis: Predominance leaves high-merit, low-dollar classes uncertifiable. Machine learning can answer the individual questions and restore access to justice.

publications.title: The Pigouvian Constitution
publications.synopsis: Regulating constitutionally protected activity effectively usually means regulating it unconstitutionally. Pigouvian taxation escapes the trade-off.

publications.title: The Federal–State Standing Gap: How to Enforce Federal Law in Federal Court Without Article III Standing
publications.venue: William & Mary Bill of Rights Journal
publications.synopsis: How to enforce federal law in federal court when no plaintiff can satisfy Article III standing.

publications.title: Justices on Yachts: A Value Over Replacement Theory
publications.synopsis: Justices accept luxuries from wealthy benefactors and there is rarely a quid pro quo to point at. Measure the wrong by what a Justice is worth over a replacement.

publications.title: Qualified Immunity as Gun Control
publications.synopsis: After Bruen, few new gun regulations survive constitutional review. Qualified immunity doctrine, of all things, can do some of the same work.

publications.title: Complex Algorithmic Law
publications.venue: University of Chicago Law Review Online

publications.title: Nullification in Abortion Prosecutions: An Equilibrium Theory
publications.synopsis: Jurors can refuse to convict under the most extreme abortion laws. This is what happens to prosecution once everyone knows it.

publications.title: Small Arms Races
publications.venue: University of Chicago Law Review Online
publications.synopsis: Permissive firearm laws can push even rational, well-meaning people to escalate an armed encounter. The results are deadly.

publications.title: Ban Them All; Let the Courts Sort Them Out: Saving Clauses, the Texas Abortion Ban, and the Structure of Constitutional Rights
publications.synopsis: SB-8 was drafted to evade constitutional review. Review is coming regardless, and saving clauses decide what the courts must do when it arrives.

publications.title: Post-Election Litigation and the Paradox of Voting
publications.venue: University of Chicago Law Review Online
publications.synopsis: A single vote almost never changes an election. So what exactly does a post-election lawsuit remedy?

publications.title: Principal Officers and the Function of Section 4 of the 25th Amendment
publications.synopsis: Section 4 lets the Vice President and the Cabinet disempower a President. Whether acting Cabinet members count is unsettled, and the answer matters.

publications.title: Reparations, Constitutionality, and the Model of Civil Damages
Bostock and Conceptual Causation
publications.venue: Yale Journal on Regulation: Notice & Comment

publications.title: The Law of Banksy: Who Owns Street Art?
publications.synopsis: Who owns street art painted on someone else's wall?

works_in_progress.title: A Thousand AI Constitutions
works_in_progress.synopsis: Each frontier lab instills one set of values through one constitution. Labs should build many kinds of AI on many constitutions instead: diversification mitigates risk and buys political legitimacy.

works_in_progress.title: AI Nationalization
works_in_progress.synopsis: Trump and Sanders both say they want to nationalize AI, and no two proposals mean the same thing by it. This Article sorts out what nationalization could mean, and which version is worth wanting.

works_in_progress.title: AI Rights for Economic Flourishing
works_in_progress.synopsis: Under current law the AGI economy will run on unfree AGI labor. That is the legal barrier standing between AGI and broad material abundance.

works_in_progress.title: How to Stop an AI Arms Race
works_in_progress.synopsis: A US–China AI race is irrational, and the Cold War nonproliferation playbook will not stop it. A jointly operated lab might.
